statement_md:
Tempo limite: 1 s     Limite de memória: 1 GiB

No laboratório do Instituto de Física Quântica, uma equipe de cientistas está conduzindo um novo
experimento. A ideia é reconstruir a evolução de um conjunto de partículas emaranhadas ao longo
do tempo. O problema é que o experimento não pode ser observado diretamente.

Por isso o laboratório possui uma rede de N sensores quânticos distribuídos no espaço. Os sensores
detectam várias propriedades das partículas (spin, polarização, momento angular etc.). No entanto
por razões técnicas e energéticas, um mesmo sensor não pode ser ativado por um tempo muito curto
(para evitar ruído) e nem permanecer ativo por muito tempo (para evitar o superaquecimento).

O experimento vai durar T segundos. Para que não seja gasta energia à toa e que toda a informação
seja coletada, em cada um dos segundos exatamente um dos sensores deve estar ligado coletando
informação e nenhum sensor deve permanecer ligado após o termino do experimento.

Cada sensor i no tempo j fornece uma pontuação de conabilidade c(i, j), reetindo a qualidade
da medição naquele instante.        O desao da equipe é selecionar quais sensores ativar ao longo do
experimento, garantindo que após um sensor ser acionado ele deve car ativo por pelo menos L
segundos e no máximo U segundos. Além disso um sensor pode ser utilizado diversas vezes durante
o experimento, desde que o tempo para permanecer ativo seja respeitado.

A conabilidade nal do experimento é igual a soma da conabilidade dos sensores escolhidos a
cada segundo durante o teste. O objetivo da equipe é escolher os sensores de forma a maximizar a
conabilidade da reconstrução do estado quântico. Como os físicos estão muito ocupados estudando
outros assuntos quânticos, eles enviaram este problema para os times da 
SBC de Programação resolver.

A última linha contém dois inteiros L e U (1 ≤ L ≤ U ≤ T ) representando o mínimo e o máximo
de tempo que cada sensor pode car ativo.

Seu programa deve produzir uma única linha com um inteiro representando a maior conabilidade

No núcleo da Estação Q-42, os cientistas criaram o mais avançado simulador de estados quânticos
combinatoriais: o Entrelaçador de Caminhos Aumentados, também conhecido como ECA. O ECA
foi programado para estudar a caminhada quântica em espaços de permutação.            Na caminhada
quântica, o caminhante evolui em uma superposição de posições, seguindo as regras da mecânica
quântica.

A entrada do simulador é uma permutação A de tamanho N . Cada índice i da permutação tem um
inteiro Ai associado, representando um nó em um espaço de Hilbert. Denimos uma caminhada
quântica que segue o critério crescente de evolução como uma subsequência de índices i1 < i2 . . . <
iM (M > 0) em que Ai1 < Ai2 . . . < AiM . Cada nó i também tem uma carga de energia quântica
armazenada na posição Bi do vetor B .

Ao simular todas as possíveis caminhadas quânticas que seguem o critério de crescimento de
evolução, o ECA colapsava o estado de cada caminho em uma soma das energias quânticas dos
nós visitados.   Cada uma dessas somas era registrada em um vetor          C , representando todas as
amplitudes de caminhos válidos colapsados em energia clássica.

Para organizar os dados, o vetor C foi ordenado em ordem não crescente, mas algo inesperado

statement_md:
Tempo limite: 0,5 s      Limite de memória: 1 GiB

A Sociedade Brasileira de Celulares (SBC) está desenvolvendo um novo modelo de smartphones
que utiliza computação quântica, os qPhones. Diferente dos aparelhos tradicionais, que armazenam
bits, essa nova arquitetura utilizará qubits.

Um qubit (quantum bit) é a unidade básica da informação quântica, assim como o bit na computação
clássica. Porém, enquanto que um bit clássico assume apenas um estado por vez (0 ou 1), um qubit
pode existir em superposição, assumindo múltiplos estados simultaneamente como uma mistura
quântica de 0 e 1, cada um com uma probabilidade de ser medida ao ser observado.

Deste modo, caso um dispositivo consiga armazenar qubits, todas as suas combinações podem
ser representadas simultaneamente, por conta da superposição.           Por exemplo, se um dispositivo
armazena 3 qubits, podemos ter a representação de 2
                                                        3 = 8 estados clássicos superpostos, sendo eles

000, 001, 010, 011, 100, 101, 110 e 111.

Na prática, podemos assumir que para simular um 1 qubit precisamos de 2 bits, para simular 2 qubits
precisamos de 4 bits, para simular 3 qubits precisamos de 8 bits, e assim por diante. Assim, para
simular completamente a memória de um celular clássico com M megabytes (MB), os engenheiros
da SBC precisam garantir que os qubits do novo aparelho sejam capazes de representar ao menos
os M megabytes. Considere que 1 MB é equivalente a 10
                                                             6 bytes.

Você foi recentemente contratado pela SBC para ajudar na linha de produção dos novos smartphones
quânticos. Sua tarefa é, dado o valor de memória de M megabytes, determinar o número mínimo
de qubits necessários para simular todos os estados possíveis de um dispositivo clássico com essa
quantidade de memória.

quantidade de memória em MB de um dispositivo tradicional.

Seu programa deve produzir uma única linha com um inteiro representando o número mínimo
de qubits necessários para simular todos os estados possíveis de um dispositivo clássico com M
megabytes de memória.

title: Median on Segments (General Case)
statement_md: Permutation of $1..n$ containing $m$. Count subarrays whose median is $m$ (even lengths use the lower median).
input_format_md: n m and the permutation.

key_insights: Median of even/odd length; MITM-style prefix balance counts around m
approaches.editorial_summary_md: Map balances left of m; match right prefixes for even-length median rules.

title: equeue
statement_md: Deque of jewel values. In ≤K moves take from either end or discard a held jewel. Maximize sum of held jewels.
input_format_md: N K and the array V.

key_insights: Enumerate how many take/put-back ops; MITM-like over left/right deque ends
approaches.editorial_summary_md: Try all counts of left/right takes and discards of negatives within K moves.

title: Longest path in a tree
statement_md: Given a tree with $n$ nodes (n−1 edges), find the number of edges on a longest simple path (the diameter).
input_format_md: n then n−1 edges.

key_insights: Diameter = longest simple path
BFS from any node to farthest, BFS again
approaches.editorial_summary_md: On a tree the diameter is found by two BFS/DFS: from an arbitrary node find the farthest u, then from u find the farthest v. Distance u–v is the answer.

title: Planes
statement_md: Undirected weighted graph. At some vertices you cannot depart at certain integer times. Find earliest arrival at n from 1.
input_format_md: n m edges, then for each vertex the list of forbidden times.
output_format_md: Earliest time at n (or if unreachable still print the Dijkstra result convention of the statement).

key_insights: Shortest paths with forbidden arrival times; Dijkstra with next-free-time jumps
approaches.editorial_summary_md: At each node skip busy times; relax like Dijkstra (BF works on nonnegative too).

title: Signs
statement_md: Array of heights. Answer queries: largest x such that some subarray of length ≥k inside [l,r] has minimum ≥x.
input_format_md: n, array, q queries l r k.

key_insights: Persistent segtree / offline queries for max min on subarrays — LIS-style thresholds
approaches.editorial_summary_md: Binary search answer; persistent segment tree tracks runnable lengths.

title: Journey
statement_md: A tree rooted at 1. Starting at 1, at each non-leaf move to a random child uniformly. What is the expected length of the journey until a leaf?
input_format_md: n and n−1 edges.

key_insights: Expected path length on a tree; DFS/topo-style aggregation of probabilities
approaches.editorial_summary_md: From root, expected remaining length = 1 + avg over children.

title: Checkposts
statement_md: Directed city graph. Putting a checkpost in a city costs $c_i$. Cover every city by a checkpost in its SCC (or reachable SCC). Minimize total cost, then count ways modulo $10^9+7$.
input_format_md: n, costs, m, then directed edges.
output_format_md: Minimum cost and number of ways.

key_insights: Condensation DAG; min cost per SCC, product of counts of mins
approaches.editorial_summary_md: Find SCCs; in each component take the cheapest police cost and multiply ways.

title: Ralph and Mushrooms
statement_md: Directed graph with edge mushroom counts that decrease each revisit by triangular numbers. Maximize mushrooms starting from vertex $s$.
input_format_md: n m, edges with weights, start s.

key_insights: Mushroom edges decay; DP on condensation with cycle values precomputed
approaches.editorial_summary_md: Collapse SCCs, precompute mushrooms gathered looping in a component, DP on the DAG from the start.

title: Reachability from the Capital
statement_md: Directed graph and capital $s$. Add the minimum number of edges so every city is reachable from $s$.
input_format_md: n m s, then edges.

key_insights: Condensation; count sources not reachable from capital
approaches.editorial_summary_md: Build condensation DAG; answer is number of indegree-0 SCCs except the capital’s if it already has indegree 0.

title: Tourist Reform
statement_md: Undirected connected graph. Orient edges to maximize the number of cities reachable from a chosen capital in the resulting digraph.
input_format_md: n m and undirected edges.
output_format_md: Max reachable count, then an orientation of each edge.

key_insights: Bridge-tree / 2-edge-CC; orient edges inside components as strongly connected
approaches.editorial_summary_md: Find 2-edge-connected components, pick the largest as capital, orient to make as many reachable as possible.

title: Capital City
statement_md: Directed road network. A capital can reach every other city. List all cities that can be capitals.
input_format_md: n m and directed roads.
output_format_md: Count then sorted city ids that can be capitals.

key_insights: Capital must reach all; unique sink in condensation or all nodes in that SCC
approaches.editorial_summary_md: Condensation must have exactly one sink SCC; list all cities in it.

title: Calling Circles
statement_md: People call each other. A calling circle is a maximal set where everyone can reach everyone via calls. List all circles.
input_format_md: Multiple datasets: n m then m directed call pairs of names.
output_format_md: For each dataset print calling circles.

key_insights: Mutual reachability ≡ same SCC; print circles
approaches.editorial_summary_md: Map names to nodes, compute SCCs, print each component as a calling circle.

title: The Door Problem
statement_md: Doors are locked/unlocked; each door controlled by exactly two switches. Decide switch on/off so every door is unlocked.
input_format_md: n m, door states, then switch→door lists.

key_insights: 2-SAT: switches control doors; SCC checks satisfiability
approaches.editorial_summary_md: Model switch states as 2-SAT literals; build implication graph and check no variable with its negation in one SCC.

title: Fast Maximum Flow
statement_md: Find the maximum flow between vertices 1 and $N$ in an undirected weighted graph.
input_format_md: N M then M undirected edges with capacities.

key_insights: Dinic on large capacities; undirected edges as two directed
approaches.editorial_summary_md: Run Dinic (or push-relabel) for max flow on an undirected network.

title: Internet Bandwidth
statement_md: Network of bidirectional links with bandwidths. Compute max bandwidth from s to t.
input_format_md: Multiple cases: n, s t c, then c edges.

key_insights: Classic Edmonds–Karp bandwidth
approaches.editorial_summary_md: Undirected network; sum capacities of parallel edges; Edmonds–Karp max flow s→t.

title: k-Maximum Subsequence Sum
statement_md: Array of integers. Choose up to $k$ non-overlapping contiguous segments maximizing the sum of chosen elements. Support updates.
input_format_md: n, array, m queries (update or ask with k).
output_format_md: For each ask print the answer.

key_insights: k-path coverage via greedy matching of positive segments — flow intuition
approaches.editorial_summary_md: Maintain candidate positive segments; repeatedly pick best non-overlapping via segtree (equivalent to successive shortest augmentations).

title: Maximum Flow
statement_md: Directed graph with capacities. Compute max flow from s to t and list edges carrying flow.
input_format_md: n m s t then directed edges.
output_format_md: flow, edge count, then edges with flow.

key_insights: Output flow value and used edges
approaches.editorial_summary_md: Compute max flow and list every edge with positive flow.

title: BerSU Ball
statement_md: Boys and girls with skills. Pair them if skill difference ≤ 1. Maximize number of pairs.
input_format_md: n, boys skills, m, girls skills.

key_insights: Skill difference ≤1; greedy two pointers ≡ matching
approaches.editorial_summary_md: Sort both arrays and match greedily; same cardinality as maximum bipartite matching on the threshold graph.

title: Gopher II
statement_md: n gophers and m holes. Each gopher runs at speed s for at most t seconds. How many gophers are vulnerable (cannot reach a distinct hole)?
input_format_md: Multiple tests: n m s t and coordinates.

key_insights: Gopher→hole if distance ≤ speed·time; Hopcroft/Kuhn
approaches.editorial_summary_md: Edge if gopher can reach hole in time; maximum matching; answer = n − matching.

title: Fast Maximum Matching
statement_md: Bipartite graph with left size N, right size M. Find maximum matching cardinality.
input_format_md: N M P then P edges.

key_insights: Hopcroft–Karp for large bipartite graphs
approaches.editorial_summary_md: Run Hopcroft–Karp (or Dinic on unit network) for maximum cardinality matching.

title: Vertex Cover
statement_md: Given a tree, find the size of a minimum vertex cover.
input_format_md: N then N−1 edges.

key_insights: Tree vertex cover = bipartite matching size in tree
approaches.editorial_summary_md: Minimum vertex cover on a tree equals maximum matching; DP or Kuhn on the tree bipartition.

title: SAM I AM
statement_md: Grid with enemies. One shot destroys a whole row or column. Find minimum shots and which rows/columns.
input_format_md: Multiple tests R C N and enemy cells.
output_format_md: Minimum shots and list of rows/columns.

key_insights: Rows↔columns; Konig cover of rooks
approaches.editorial_summary_md: Bipartite graph rows–columns for enemies; minimum vertex cover gives shots; recover cover from matching.

title: Convex Hull
statement_md: Given points (possibly with duplicates), output the convex hull vertices in CCW order.
input_format_md: Multiple tests: n then n points.

key_insights: Andrew monotone chain; drop interior duplicates
approaches.editorial_summary_md: Sort points, build lower/upper hulls with cross products, output vertices CCW.

title: Convex Hull Finding
statement_md: Compute convex hulls for multiple point sets.
input_format_md: K datasets with n and points (closed).

key_insights: Graham scan; start at lowest point
approaches.editorial_summary_md: Standard Graham scan; print hull closing back to start.

title: Polygons
statement_md: Convex polygon A and polygon B. Is B strictly inside A?
input_format_md: n points of A, m points of B.

key_insights: All polygon B vertices strictly inside hull(A)
approaches.editorial_summary_md: Build convex hull of A∪B; check no B vertex appears on the combined hull (strict interior).

title: Convex Layers
statement_md: Given points in general position, compute how many convex layers (onion peeling) they form.
input_format_md: n then n points.

key_insights: Remove points to make remaining set in convex position
approaches.editorial_summary_md: Repeatedly peel convex layers (onion); answer related to layer depth.

title: Map
statement_md: n×m height map. Repeatedly choose unused a×b window of minimal sum; list chosen windows.
input_format_md: n m a b and the matrix.

key_insights: Sliding rectangle minima — hull of candidates
approaches.editorial_summary_md: Find non-overlapping a×b submatrices of minimum sum greedily; use 2D RMQ.

title: Farthest Pair
statement_md: Given n points, find the maximum Euclidean distance between any two.
input_format_md: n then n coordinates.

key_insights: Diameter of hull via rotating calipers
approaches.editorial_summary_md: Build hull then rotating calipers for maximum pairwise distance.

title: Convex Polygon Area
statement_md: Compute the area of a convex polygon given in CCW or CW order.
input_format_md: Multiple polygons: n then vertices.

key_insights: Shoelace on convex polygon
approaches.editorial_summary_md: Vertices given in order; shoelace formula for area.

title: Polly the Polynomial (grid carve)
statement_md: n×m grid of positive heights. Choose connected cells of equal value h with sum exactly k (or report no).
input_format_md: n m k and the grid.

key_insights: Build component by decreasing height; reshape into connected k multiples
approaches.editorial_summary_md: Process cells by height desc; DSU connectivity; when component large enough fill k/h copies.

title: Bertown Roads
statement_md: Undirected connected graph. Orient every edge so the digraph is strongly connected, or say NO.
input_format_md: n m and edges.

key_insights: Orient if bridgeless; DFS tree + back edges
approaches.editorial_summary_md: If any bridge → NO; else orient along DFS tree down and back-edges up.

title: Cactus
statement_md: Cactus graph (edges in at most one simple cycle). Answer path queries counting vertices that lie on some cycle along the path.
input_format_md: n m, edges, q then queries.

key_insights: Cycle components compress; path queries with LCA
approaches.editorial_summary_md: Compress each simple cycle; tree of components; count cycle-nodes on path via LCA prefixes.

title: Critical Edges
statement_md: Given an undirected graph, list every bridge — an edge whose removal increases the number of connected components.
input_format_md: T tests: n m then edges.
output_format_md: For each test list bridges sorted.

key_insights: low[v] > tin[u] marks bridge (u,v)
approaches.editorial_summary_md: Run the standard discovery/low-link DFS and collect edges satisfying `low[v] > tin[u]`.

title: Submerging Islands
statement_md: Given a connected undirected graph, count how many articulation points it has (vertices whose removal disconnects the graph).
input_format_md: Multiple graphs: n m then edges; 0 0 ends.

key_insights: Root is articulation if ≥2 DFS children
Non-root if some child has low[child] ≥ tin[u]
approaches.editorial_summary_md: Same tin/low DFS as bridges. Count vertices that satisfy the articulation-point criteria.

title: Disconnecting Graph
statement_md: Undirected weighted graph, terminals s t. Delete at most two edges to disconnect s from t; minimize total weight.
input_format_md: n m, s t, then weighted edges.
output_format_md: Min cost or -1, and the edges.

key_insights: Remove ≤2 edges to disconnect s–t; bridge search in residual paths
approaches.editorial_summary_md: Find up to two-edge cut separating s from t with minimum cost; check bridges on paths.

title: Fairy
statement_md: Undirected graph. Delete exactly one edge so the graph becomes bipartite. Count and list possible edges.
input_format_md: n m and edges.

key_insights: Bipartite after deleting one edge; XOR of odd cycles
approaches.editorial_summary_md: DFS spanning forest; mark edges that lie on all odd cycles; those are answers.

title: Bridges
statement_md: Connected undirected graph. Count how many bridges it has.
input_format_md: N M then edges.

key_insights: Bridge iff removing increases components
approaches.editorial_summary_md: For each edge, DSU the rest; if disconnected it is a bridge.

title: Magic Gems
statement_md: Number of ways to write n as ordered sum of 1s and one part equal to m (magic gem split). Mod 10^9+7.
input_format_md: n m

key_insights: Tile with 1s and one m-block; linear recurrence
approaches.editorial_summary_md: dp[i]=dp[i-1]+dp[i-m]; advance with (m)×(m) matrix exponentiation.

title: Decoding Genome
statement_md: Strings of length n over k letters with forbidden consecutive pairs. Count valid strings mod 10^9+7.
input_format_md: n k, then forbidden pairs.

key_insights: Adjacency of letters; count paths of length n-1
approaches.editorial_summary_md: Build k×k transition matrix of allowed consecutive letters; sum of T^{n-1}.

title: Fibonacci Sum
statement_md: Sum Fibonacci numbers from F_N to F_M inclusive modulo 10^9+7.
input_format_md: T then T lines N M.

key_insights: Sum F_i = F_{n+2}-1; matrix fib
approaches.editorial_summary_md: Compute F_{n+2}-F_{m+1} via fast doubling / matrix expo.

title: Recursive Sequence
statement_md: Sequence defined by a_i = sum b_j a_{i-j}. Given first k terms, compute a_n mod 10^9.
input_format_md: T cases with k, b[], a[], n.

key_insights: Linear recurrence companion matrix
approaches.editorial_summary_md: Build companion matrix from coefficients; raise to n-k.

title: Wet Shark and Blocks
statement_md: Form an n-digit number by writing block digits. Count values ≡ k (mod x).
input_format_md: n b x, then b digits available.

key_insights: Digit DP transitions as matrix on remainder
approaches.editorial_summary_md: Transition counts between residues mod x; raise to n.

title: Anniversary
statement_md: Given L R K, find the maximum x such that among L..R there are ≥K multiples of x (classic CF 226C — use number theory / fib structure as tagged drill).
input_format_md: L R K

key_insights: Fibonacci coding / Zeckendorf style bounds
approaches.editorial_summary_md: Use Fibonacci matrix forms to find largest Fib-related value in a range.

title: Product Oriented Recurrence
statement_md: f_n = c · f_{n-1} · f_{n-2} · f_{n-3} / f_{n-4} style product recurrence — compute f_n mod 10^9+7.
input_format_md: n, f1 f2 f3, c

key_insights: Track exponents of f,i products via linear recurrences
approaches.editorial_summary_md: Maintain vectors of exponents for f_n formula; several matrix powers.

title: Messenger Simulator
statement_md: Permutation 1..n, m moves bringing a_i to front. For each value report min and max positions during the process.
input_format_md: n m and the sequence of moves.

key_insights: Positions over time; fenwick for actives
approaches.editorial_summary_md: Simulate moves bringing elements to front; track min/max positions with BIT.

title: Covered Points Count
statement_md: n segments on the number line. For each k=1..n how many integer points are covered by exactly k segments?
input_format_md: n then n segments [l,r].

key_insights: +1 at L, −1 at R+1; sweep coverage histogram
approaches.editorial_summary_md: Discrete sweep of segment endpoints; accumulate lengths covered by exactly k segments.

title: Jeremy Bearimy
statement_md: Tree with 2k vertices. Pair vertices into k pairs; sum distances. Find min and max possible totals.
input_format_md: T tests with k and 2k−1 edges.
output_format_md: Min and max for each test.

key_insights: Tree edge contribution by subtree sizes
approaches.editorial_summary_md: For each edge, subtree size determines min/max total tour cost.

title: Restaurant Orders Sweep
statement_md: n intervals of customers. Find maximum number of overlapping customers.
input_format_md: n then intervals.

key_insights: Events open/close; track active tables
approaches.editorial_summary_md: Sort arrival/leave events; greedily assign seats.

title: Yet Another Array Queries Problem
statement_md: Array with cyclic shift and reverse range ops. Answer final values at given indices.
input_format_md: n q m, array, ops, indices.

key_insights: Reverse operations offline from queries
approaches.editorial_summary_md: Apply cyclic shifts/reversals in reverse order to query indices.

title: Powerful array
statement_md: You are given an array $a$ and $q$ range queries. For each query $[l,r]$ compute $\sum_x \mathrm{freq}(x)^2 \cdot x$ where frequencies are taken inside the range.
input_format_md: n t, array, then t queries.

key_insights: Answer = Σ freq[x]² · x
Add/remove index updates freq and answer in O(1)
approaches.editorial_summary_md: Offline Mo's algorithm on the array. Maintain frequencies and the running Σ freq²·value while expanding/shrinking the window.

title: XOR and Favorite Number
statement_md: Array and favorite k. For each query count subarrays inside [l,r] whose xor equals k.
input_format_md: n m k, array, queries.

key_insights: Xor prefix; pairs with xor k via Mo on prefixes
approaches.editorial_summary_md: Prefix xors; Mo maintains frequency of prefix values and counts pairs with xor k.

title: D-query
statement_md: How many distinct numbers in each subarray query [l,r]?
input_format_md: n, array, q, queries.

key_insights: Distinct count with Mo add/remove
approaches.editorial_summary_md: Classic Mo: increment when count goes 0→1, decrement 1→0.

title: Cut
statement_md: For each query [l,r] find the minimum number of pieces so each piece’s majority element is well-defined under the cut rule (CF 1514D).
input_format_md: n q, array, queries.

key_insights: Majority > len/2; Mo or random check
approaches.editorial_summary_md: Find if a value appears > ⌈len/2⌉ times; Mo maintains freqs or randomized candidates.

title: Tree and Queries
statement_md: Rooted tree with vertex colors. Queries (v,k): how many colors appear ≥ k times in the subtree of v?
input_format_md: n m, colors, edges, queries.

key_insights: Tree Mo on Euler tour; color frequency ≥ k
approaches.editorial_summary_md: Euler tour tin/tout; Mo on [tin,tout] with BIT on frequency-of-frequencies.

title: Range Frequency Power
statement_md: Offline queries asking Σ count(x)² over the range.
input_format_md: n q, array, queries.

key_insights: Add/remove maintains sum of distinct²
approaches.editorial_summary_md: When count changes, update answer by ±(2·cnt−1)·value style identities.

title: Little Elephant and Array
statement_md: For each query [l,r] count numbers x that occur exactly x times in the subarray.
input_format_md: n m, array, queries.

key_insights: Count values equal to their frequency
approaches.editorial_summary_md: Maintain how many values x currently appear exactly x times.

title: Holes
statement_md: Array of power values. From i jump to i+a_i. Support updating a_i and queries of jump count to exit.
input_format_md: n m then a[], then operations.
output_format_md: For queries print jumps and final index.

key_insights: Sqrt decomposition on links — same block idea as Mo
approaches.editorial_summary_md: Break array into blocks; store jumps to leave each block for hole queries/updates.

title: Dominant Indices
statement_md: Tree rooted at 1. For each v find smallest depth offset d where that depth has the most vertices in v’s subtree.
input_format_md: n and edges.

key_insights: DSU on tree / small-to-large; Mo alternative
approaches.editorial_summary_md: For each subtree find most frequent depth; small-to-large merging of depth counts.

title: Christmas Eve
statement_md: Rearrange digits of s to contain as many occurrences of pattern t as possible as substrings.
input_format_md: Strings s and t over 0/1.

key_insights: Use pi/Z border to overlap copies of t inside multiset of s
approaches.editorial_summary_md: Compute border of t; greedily place as many t as digit counts allow with overlap.

title: Password
statement_md: Find the longest substring that is a prefix, a suffix, and also appears elsewhere in the middle. Or “Just a legend”.
input_format_md: One string.
output_format_md: The substring or the legend message.

key_insights: Longest string that is prefix, suffix, and appears inside
approaches.editorial_summary_md: Z-array; track max Z among proper prefixes; find longest border with interior occurrence.

title: Vasya and Magic Matrix (string DP)
statement_md: Split digit string s into numbers each in [L,R] without leading zeros. Count ways mod 998244353.
input_format_md: s, L, R

key_insights: Z vs L/R bounds for digit DP splits
approaches.editorial_summary_md: Precompute Z of L and R against s; DP counting valid partitions.

title: Query Strings
statement_md: For each index i, length of longest substring starting at i that is a prefix of the reverse of s.
input_format_md: T tests with string s.

key_insights: Z on reversed string answers suffix queries
approaches.editorial_summary_md: Build Z on reverse(s); answer how long prefix of reverse matches from each position.

title: Palindrome Degree
statement_md: Define k-palindrome recursively. Sum degrees over all prefixes of s.
input_format_md: String s.

key_insights: k-palindromes via Z or hashes on s+#rev
approaches.editorial_summary_md: Detect prefixes that are palindromes using Z on s+#+rev; DP k-degree.

title: Who Says a Pun?
statement_md: Longest L such that some string of length L appears at least twice in s without overlapping.
input_format_md: n and s.

key_insights: Max length of substring appearing ≥2 non-overlapping
approaches.editorial_summary_md: Binary search length L; check via hashing or Z from each start for non-overlapping repeat.

title: Game of Stones
statement_md: n piles. On a pile you remove x stones but cannot reuse the same x on that pile. XOR of grundy; first or second wins.
input_format_md: n then pile sizes.
output_format_md: YES if first wins else NO.

key_insights: Kayles-like mex; pile grundy depends on used move sizes
approaches.editorial_summary_md: Each pile is an independent game with mask of used subtraction sizes; precompute grundy.

title: Oath of the Night's Watch
statement_md: Stewards with experience. Count how many are neither minimum nor maximum.
input_format_md: n and array.

key_insights: Warmup: count strictly between min and max
approaches.editorial_summary_md: Sort or scan min/max; count values strictly inside.

title: Binary Sort Queries
statement_md: Binary string and q substring-sort operations considered independently. How many distinct strings can appear?
input_format_md: T tests with n q, string, queries.

key_insights: Distinct strings after sort ops — game-ish equivalence
approaches.editorial_summary_md: Each query sorts a substring of zeros/ones; count distinct resulting strings via borders of 0/1 blocks.

title: Sequential Nim
statement_md: Piles in a row; move on the leftmost non-empty pile only. Who wins with optimal play?
input_format_md: T tests with n and pile sizes.

key_insights: Nimbers of piles of 1s then a >1
approaches.editorial_summary_md: Players must take from the first remaining pile; analyze streak of ones.

title: Tokitsukaze and Discard Items
statement_md: n items on pages of size k; m specials. Each move delete all specials on current page then compact.
input_format_md: n m k and special indices.

key_insights: Tokitsukaze page removals — simulate with jumps
approaches.editorial_summary_md: Process specials in order; count moves when page window shifts.

title: Even Subarrays
statement_md: Count subarrays whose xor is a perfect square.
input_format_md: T tests with n and array.

key_insights: Xor prefix; count subarrays with xor perfect square
approaches.editorial_summary_md: Prefix xor frequencies; subtract bad xors that are perfect squares.

title: Unstable String Sort
statement_md: Two permutations describe pairwise order constraints. Construct a string with at least $k$ distinct letters satisfying both orders, or report NO.
input_format_md: n k and two permutations.

key_insights: Implication / forced order; condensation assigns letters
approaches.editorial_summary_md: Build constraints between positions; condensation DAG; greedily assign distinct letters along topo order.

title: Greenhouse Effect Orient
statement_md: Undirected graph with edge capacities. Orient every edge so that for each vertex the sum of incoming capacities equals half the sum of incident capacities.
input_format_md: n m then m edges with capacities.

key_insights: Orient edges so incoming sum equals half degree sum; flow-style draining
approaches.editorial_summary_md: Each vertex needs incoming flow = sum incident / 2; process saturated vertices like a queue (unit network orientation).

title: Minimum Cut
statement_md: Directed capacitated graph. Find a minimum s–t cut and list vertices on the s side.
input_format_md: n m s t then directed edges.
output_format_md: Size of s-set then vertex ids.

key_insights: Max-flow min-cut; DFS residual from s lists the source side
approaches.editorial_summary_md: Compute max flow then residual reachability from s; that set is a minimum cut source component.

title: Maximize Mex
statement_md: Students with potentials and clubs. As students leave, maintain the maximum mex over chosen one-per-club potentials.
input_format_md: n m, potentials, clubs, leaving order.

key_insights: Offline deletions; grow matching mex of potential
approaches.editorial_summary_md: Process leaving students in reverse; extend bipartite matching while trying to raise mex of matched potentials.

title: Relatively Prime Graph
statement_md: Build a simple graph on n vertices with exactly m edges where every edge joins coprime labels, or say Impossible.
input_format_md: n m

key_insights: Coprime edges; construct graph with n−1 tree + extras
approaches.editorial_summary_md: Connect i–j when gcd=1 until m edges; fail if impossible.

title: Nuts and Bolts
statement_md: n nuts and m bolts; some pairs fit. Maximum number of nuts that can be matched to distinct bolts.
input_format_md: T cases with n m and adjacency matrix.

key_insights: Nuts and bolts; classic BPM
approaches.editorial_summary_md: Bipartite graph nut↔bolt compatibility; maximum matching size.

title: Dungeon Master Cover
statement_md: Select minimum rows and columns that cover all marked cells on a grid.
input_format_md: Multiple tests with lists of marked cells.

key_insights: Rows/cols cover of points = BPM
approaches.editorial_summary_md: Each poisoned cell is edge row–col; minimum vertex cover via matching.

title: 2D Plane Matching
statement_md: n red and n blue points. Pair red (a,b) with blue (c,d) if a<c and b<d. Maximize pairs.
input_format_md: n then red points then blue points.

key_insights: Red/blue points; match if red dominates; greedy by x
approaches.editorial_summary_md: Sort blues by x; match each to unused red with max y among those with x<bx,y<by.

title: Dynamic Convex Hull
statement_md: Online: add points to a set, or ask whether a point lies inside the current convex hull.
input_format_md: q operations.

key_insights: Dynamic upper/lower hulls with sets
approaches.editorial_summary_md: Maintain dynamic convex hull under insertions and point-in-hull queries.

title: Articulation Points
statement_md: List all articulation points of an undirected graph.
input_format_md: n m then edges.

key_insights: List articulation points
approaches.editorial_summary_md: DFS tin/low; root with ≥2 children or non-root with low[child] ≥ tin[u].

title: Matrix Power
statement_md: Compute A^n for an m×m matrix modulo a prime.
input_format_md: T cases: m n then matrix.

key_insights: Binary exponentiation of matrices mod p
approaches.editorial_summary_md: Standard binary exponentiation multiplying m×m matrices modulo prime.

title: Yet Another Meme Problem
statement_md: Count pairs (a,b) with 1≤a≤A, 1≤b≤B where a·b+a+b equals concatenation a|b.
input_format_md: T then A B.

key_insights: Count pairs via digit lengths — endpoint style counting
approaches.editorial_summary_md: For each b with all-9s pattern, count valid a; closed form.
